candidates.next_evidence: Verify 2026 production guidance, unit cash costs, Grasberg operating status, reserve life, smelter/refining integration, customer contract structure, and sensitivity to copper prices versus volume growth.
candidates.node_relation: Direct copper producer with large-scale mined copper exposure; copper is a primary input for grids, electrical equipment, cabling, data-center power systems, motors, renewables, and electrification infrastructure.
candidates.theme_relation: High direct exposure to the energy-electrification materials bottleneck because grid expansion and data-center electrical infrastructure raise copper intensity across multiple demand nodes.
candidates.why_include: Obvious leader for US-listed copper exposure. Freeport states it is a leading copper producer and supplied about 7% of global mined copper in 2025, making it a direct candidate for copper-scarcity monitoring.

candidates.next_evidence: Check 2026 and 2027 production guidance, ore-grade decline risk, Peru and Mexico permitting, capital expenditure timing, reserve quality, smelter/refinery bottlenecks, and cost inflation.
candidates.node_relation: Direct copper producer with mining and processing operations in Peru and Mexico; copper output links to grid wiring, transformers, renewables, EVs, motors, and industrial electrification.
candidates.theme_relation: A second large public-market mapping for the copper chokepoint, especially relevant if global copper mine supply falls short of grid and electrification demand.
candidates.why_include: Southern Copper reported 2025 copper production of 954,270 tons and is one of the more direct US-listed copper supply exposures. It also provides useful evidence on ore grades, project pipeline, and Latin America permitting/geopolitical risk.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify GOES and NOES revenue contribution, domestic market share, transformer-customer contracts, exposure to DOE efficiency rules, import competition, production capacity, and whether electrical steel is material enough to move consolidated earnings.
candidates.node_relation: Electrical steel producer with exposure to grain-oriented electrical steel used in transformer cores and non-oriented electrical steel used in motors and electrified equipment.
candidates.theme_relation: Maps to the transformer and motor-material bottleneck. GOES is a critical input for power and distribution transformers, where long lead times and component shortages are constraining grid expansion and data-center interconnection.
candidates.why_include: Cleveland-Cliffs is one of the few US-listed ways to study North American electrical-steel exposure. Its annual-report language references grain-oriented electrical steel demand tied to the grid and transformer market, but the exact earnings sensitivity needs segment-level validation.

candidates.next_evidence: Track lithium price realization, Energy Storage segment margins, volume guidance, contract indexation, project curtailments, inventory write-downs, and whether stationary storage demand offsets EV-cycle weakness.
candidates.node_relation: Lithium producer and processor supplying battery materials used in EVs and stationary energy storage; storage is a second-order input for renewables integration and grid flexibility.
candidates.theme_relation: Adjacent critical-mineral exposure. Lithium is less directly tied to transformers/copper than FCX/SCCO/CLF, but it is relevant to grid storage, EV electrification, and renewable-energy balancing.
candidates.why_include: Albemarle’s Energy Storage business gives direct lithium exposure, and company materials cite long-term demand from stationary storage and EVs. Inclusion is warranted, but lithium pricing oversupply/undersupply cycles make the chokepoint claim more conditional.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify commercial magnet ramp, customer qualification, DoD/DoW agreement economics, Apple/GM offtake details, heavy rare-earth feedstock availability, Chinese supply-chain exposure, and whether magnet volumes become material to revenue.
candidates.node_relation: Rare-earth materials and magnet producer tied to NdPr, Dy/Tb, and NdFeB permanent magnets used in electric motors, robotics, defense systems, wind-related equipment, and electrified motion.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Rare earth mining, separation, and magnet manufacturing
candidates.theme_relation: Specialty-component and critical-materials exposure. Rare-earth magnets are not the same chokepoint as copper or GOES, but they are a scarce, geopolitically concentrated input for electrified motors and some clean-energy/industrial systems.
candidates.why_include: MP Materials reports vertically integrated rare-earth capabilities from mining and processing to magnet manufacturing, produced record NdPr oxide in 2025, and is scaling US magnet capacity. This makes it a plausible specialty-material chokepoint candidate.

evidence.claim: IEA’s Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025 identifies copper demand growth from expanding construction, grid electrification, and industrial equipment, and warns that the current mine-project pipeline points to a potential copper supply shortfall by 2035.
evidence.source_title: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025 - Executive summary

evidence.claim: The US Department of Energy describes distribution transformers as basic grid building blocks facing supply-chain constraints, long lead times, and component shortages.
Freeport-McMoRan states it is a leading copper producer and supplied about 7% of the world’s mined copper in 2025.
Southern Copper reported 2025 copper production of 954,270 tons in its fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results.
evidence.source_title: Southern Copper Corporation Fourth Quarter and Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: Cleveland-Cliffs’ annual report references grain-oriented electrical steel and transformer-related demand, supporting its inclusion as a possible electrical-steel exposure for grid bottleneck research.
Albemarle’s Q4 2025 materials identify long-term growth drivers from stationary storage and EV demand, with lithium demand expected to grow year over year in 2026.
MP Materials reported record 2025 NdPr oxide production, first NdFeB magnets on commercial equipment, and a Texas incentive package for a new magnetics facility.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: MP Materials announced a public-private partnership intended to expand US rare-earth magnet manufacturing capacity to an estimated 10,000 metric tons once the new facility is completed.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Announces Transformational Public-Private Partnership with the Department of Defense

memory_update.text: FCX and SCCO should be treated as the two cleanest US-listed direct copper producers for the critical-materials node.
CLF is a potentially important electrical-steel mapping, but its chokepoint relevance depends on verifying GOES/NOES revenue materiality, transformer exposure, and capacity constraints.
ALB is an adjacent battery-minerals exposure for grid storage and EV electrification, but current lithium-cycle economics must be checked before treating it as a live bottleneck beneficiary.

MP is a specialty-materials and magnet candidate tied to rare-earth supply-chain localization, but the key research variable is whether magnet capacity ramps into material revenue and margin contribution.

This pass did not include private or foreign-primary leaders such as Southwire, Prysmian, Nucor affiliates, POSCO, Nippon Steel, or major non-US copper miners unless US-listed exposure was clear. A later global/ADR pass should cover these gaps.

node: Critical materials for electrification: copper, electrical steel, battery minerals, and specialty components
summary: Expanded the universe around the critical-materials input node for electrification. The strongest US-listed candidates for this pass are direct producers of copper, grain-oriented/electrical steel, lithium, and rare-earth magnet materials. Copper and electrical steel screen as higher-conviction chokepoint inputs because they map directly into grids, transformers, substations, motors, renewables, and data-center power distribution. Lithium and rare-earth magnets are included as adjacent critical-material exposures tied to grid storage, EVs, electrified motion, and energy infrastructure, but require closer evidence on pricing, contract structure, and end-market mix.
